body:
CONTEXT. ADR-0015's objective is eliminating the structural merge conflict in .adlc/manifest.jsonl via a segmented (chain forest) format under .adlc/manifest.d/. The runtime dispatch for that format is fully built: ten production boundaries across seven files branch on isSegmentedRepo() (packages/gate-manifest/lib/record.mjs, packages/gate-manifest/lib/segment-writer.mjs, packages/tickets/lib/evidence.mjs, packages/tickets/lib/doctor.mjs, packages/tickets/lib/manifest-segments.mjs readOwnChains, packages/ticket-sync/lib/reassign.mjs, packages/fleet/lib/complete.mjs), and the suite exercises both branches. But NOTHING in shipped code writes the activation marker (.adlc/manifest.d/.store.json, format 'adlc-manifest-segments', version 1) — only tests do. Segmented mode is therefore unreachable in every real repository, and the ADR's documented weekly conflict cost continues unabated. This ticket makes the storage mode an explicit, supported, per-repository choice and provides the missing greenfield activation path.

DESIGN STANCE. Single-file mode is a PERMANENT supported mode, not a pre-migration legacy state. Repositories with low parallelism keep the simpler single file indefinitely; repositories doing parallel worktree fan-out opt into forest mode. Mode is detected per-repo from the marker exactly as the dispatch sites already do; no configuration file, no environment variable, no new detection mechanism. The history-preserving cutover for a repo with an EXISTING non-empty root manifest.jsonl (freeze root, first segment anchors to root tail) is deliberately OUT of this ticket — it remains T-MANIFEST-FOREST-MIGRATE's scope. This ticket ships only the greenfield path: enabling forest mode in a repo whose root manifest is absent or empty.

WORK ITEM 1 — `adlc gate-manifest enable` subcommand. New lib module packages/gate-manifest/lib/enable.mjs wired into packages/gate-manifest/bin/gate-manifest.mjs. Behavior: (a) dry-run by default per repo convention — print the plan (marker path, marker content, current mode) and write nothing; --write performs it; (b) greenfield only: if a non-empty .adlc/manifest.jsonl root exists, exit 2 with an error naming the cutover ceremony (T-MANIFEST-FOREST-MIGRATE) as the path for repos with history — never write the marker over a live root; an absent or zero-entry root is greenfield and proceeds; (c) idempotent: if isSegmentedRepo() is already true, exit 0 without rewriting the marker (report already enabled); if manifest.d/ exists with segments but no valid marker, exit 2 (broken state to surface, not silently repair — mirrors init's handling of pre-existing broken stores); (d) creates .adlc/manifest.d/ and writes the marker atomically (temp file + rename, matching the store's other atomic writers); (e) --json output for orchestration (exactly ONE JSON document on stdout in both dry-run and --write modes); (f) committability check: before writing (and as part of the dry-run plan), verify the marker path is not gitignored — probe git check-ignore with a trailing-slash directory path on dry-run (the directory may not exist yet; a bare-path probe on a missing directory false-passes) and against the real path under --write; if ignored, exit 2 with the exact negation lines to add (!.adlc/manifest.d/ and !.adlc/manifest.d/**) — an ignored marker silently reverts every OTHER checkout to single-file mode, which is per-checkout evidence divergence, the failure this feature exists to prevent; (g) workspace precondition: if no .adlc/ directory exists, exit 2 pointing at adlc-init — never create a workspace as a side effect; (h) decision order is load-bearing: isSegmentedRepo() FIRST (it is true for the marker OR a cutover-tailed root, so a repo that cut over but lost its marker reports already-enabled/exit 0 rather than being told to re-run a ceremony it already ran), then the broken-state check, then the live-root refusal, then greenfield. The frozen rail on this ticket pins record.mjs byte-identical. segment-writer.mjs and evidence.mjs were released from rails (second authorized narrowing) to implement two adversarial-review round-5 fixes at their correct layer: write-side recovery is KEY-GATED and signature-verified, mirroring readOwnChains (a keyless writer mints fresh and writes its token — recovering a segment the keyless reader would then refuse to read stranded the checkout loudly and permanently); and both producers refuse at MINT time when the actual branch-derived segment filename is gitignored, failing before any local-only evidence is recorded. lineage.mjs and the tickets-package manifest-segments.mjs are NOT rails: this ticket also lands the write-side lineage-recovery fix from T-01KYTQ4BADHSDJNBFNZHB2ZG5V (gap 1) in both files, so activation and fresh-clone write recovery ship as one self-consistent unit — adversarial review established that activating forest mode while the spec records gap 1 open contradicts the threat model, which lists a lost lineage token on a fresh clone as in scope. enable.mjs imports markerPath/isSegmentedRepo from lib/lineage.mjs rather than duplicating path or format constants.

WORK ITEM 2 — spec reframe (docs/specs/segmented-gate-manifest.md). Rewrite the mode-selection framing: add a 'Storage modes' section early in the spec stating both modes are first-class and permanent; single-file is the default and remains fully supported; forest is opt-in via `adlc gate-manifest enable` (greenfield) or the cutover ceremony (repos with history, T-MANIFEST-FOREST-MIGRATE); mode detection is the marker, per section 4.7. Remove or rephrase language presenting single-file as merely 'legacy' or a pre-cutover state, except where 'root segment' terminology genuinely refers to the frozen root inside an already-segmented repo. Compaction/downgrade remains an ADR non-goal; state that the mode choice is one-way for now.

WORK ITEM 3 — threat model section in the same spec. Add an explicit 'Threat model' section recording the maintainer's decision on adversary scope. In scope: accidental corruption, concurrent-writer races, lost or stale lineage tokens, honest-mistake divergence, and tamper-EVIDENCE — detecting after the fact that committed evidence bytes changed, via hash chains and (when ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY is set) HMAC provenance. Out of scope: an adversary holding repository commit access but NOT the manifest key who plants, renames, or forges manifest content designed to be trusted — commit access to the repository is treated as trusted for manifest purposes; resisting malicious committers is explicitly a non-goal (they can already alter the code the evidence describes, so the manifest cannot be a stronger trust root than the tree it lives in). The section must state plainly that existing hardening already merged (signature-verified recovery, fail-closed ambiguity refusals, unsigned-entry rejection) is RETAINED — this section changes no runtime behavior; it records scope for future design work on this spec's mechanisms. Do not include any language that instructs, pre-classifies, or otherwise addresses reviews or reviewers; state the scope decision in design terms only.

WORK ITEM 4 — document the accepted limitation of forest-mode recovery. In the spec's gap list (section 4.4a area), re-scope gap 3 from open-design-work to accepted limitation, citing the threat model: branch-name reuse after a merged branch's deletion, and detached-HEAD checkouts with committed segments, can make token-less recovery surface or refuse on a semantically unrelated lineage's segment. Under the recorded threat model this is an accuracy edge accepted for now: the failure modes are visible (fail-closed refusal) or benign-stale (reading a merged lineage's evidence), not silent corruption, and the conjunction of preconditions (forest mode enabled, token lost, exact-name reuse, segment still in tree) is rare relative to the weekly conflict cost forest mode removes. Record that revisiting requires git-ancestry-aware identity plus segment lifecycle (close-on-merge), per the existing design note in section 7 point 1.

DOCS. Update docs/tools/gate-manifest.md with the enable subcommand (flags, exit codes, greenfield restriction, pointer to the cutover ticket for repos with history).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.
AC1 — greenfield enable works end to end: in a git repo fixture with no root manifest (and separately, an empty one), `gate-manifest enable --write` creates .adlc/manifest.d/.store.json; isSegmentedRepo() returns true in BOTH packages (gate-manifest lib/lineage.mjs AND the tickets-package twin in lib/manifest-segments.mjs — cross-package recognition is asserted, not assumed); a subsequent appendManifestEntry writes to a segment, not root. Verify: new tests in packages/gate-manifest/test/ exercising the real CLI entry (spawn the bin) and the lib function; node --test packages/gate-manifest/test/.
AC2 — live-root refusal: with a non-empty root manifest.jsonl, enable exits 2, writes nothing (no manifest.d/ created, no marker), and the error names the cutover ceremony. Verify: test asserting exit code, empty filesystem effect, and message content.
AC3 — dry-run default: without --write, nothing is created and the plan prints. Verify: test asserting no filesystem change.
AC4 — idempotency and broken-state refusal: enable on an already-enabled repo exits 0 leaving the marker bytes unchanged; enable with manifest.d/ present containing segments but no valid marker exits 2; enable on a repo whose root ends in a cutover entry but whose marker is missing exits 0 as already-enabled (isSegmentedRepo is true via the cutover tail). Verify: tests asserting marker bytes identical (before/after read) and exit codes.
AC5 — spec passes lint after the rewrite: adlc spec-lint docs/specs/segmented-gate-manifest.md exits 0. Verify: run the command.
AC6 — threat model present and behavior-neutral: the spec contains a 'Threat model' section naming the in-scope and out-of-scope adversaries above; the full suite passes unchanged, demonstrating no runtime behavior change rode along. Verify: grep -q '## Threat model' docs/specs/segmented-gate-manifest.md && npm test.
AC7 — rails hold: the rail file is byte-identical to base. Verify: git diff --exit-code origin/main -- packages/gate-manifest/lib/record.mjs.
AC8 — full suite green and mutation-gate clean: npm test passes; node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12 reports no surviving mutants in the changed code.
AC9 — trust-root prosecution: packages/gate-manifest is trust-root tier, so P5 requires a distinct-provider cross-model review approve bound to the reviewed revision. Verify: adlc prosecute --base main exits 0 on the implementation branch.
AC10 — gitignore safety: in a fixture whose .gitignore contains .adlc/* with NO manifest.d negations, enable exits 2 in both dry-run and --write modes and creates nothing; with the negation lines present (or no .gitignore at all), enable proceeds. Verify: tests covering both fixtures, asserting exit codes and zero filesystem effect on refusal.
AC11 — single-document --json: JSON.parse of the full stdout succeeds for enable --json in both dry-run and --write modes. Verify: test asserting parseability of entire stdout.

RELATED: the init-defaults root cause (ADLC_GITIGNORE_LINES omits the manifest negations entirely, so init-scaffolded repos never commit manifest.jsonl either) is a separate bug ticket in this store fixing packages/init/lib/gitignore-defaults.mjs; this ticket only refuses cleanly when it detects the condition.
AC12 — write-side recovery (carried from T-01KYTQ4BADHSDJNBFNZHB2ZG5V AC1/AC2): a fresh clone whose first action is a REAL write through the production producer extends the branch's committed segment (no duplicate mint), pre-clone evidence stays visible to a real consumer read afterwards, recovery never writes the .lineage token, and genuine ambiguity refuses through the producer without minting. Verify: node --test packages/gate-manifest/test/segment-writer.test.mjs packages/tickets/test/manifest-segments.test.mjs --test-name-pattern=AC12.
AC13 — write-side authentication symmetry: a fresh keyless clone (key null) whose first action is a write FAILS CLOSED when a committed same-branch segment exists — never extends (the keyless reader refuses recovered content, stranding the checkout) and never shadow-mints (a fresh token would hide the committed evidence from every later read); keyless greenfield writes mint normally. A KEYED writer refuses an unauthenticatable single candidate, including a branch claim riding a v1 signature (v1 does not cover branch/anchor, so identity must be v2-authenticated on the branch-bearing first entry). Verify: node --test packages/gate-manifest/test/segment-writer.test.mjs packages/tickets/test/manifest-segments.test.mjs --test-name-pattern=AC13.
AC15 — persisted authentication mode: activation without a key refuses unless --allow-keyless opts in deliberately (keyless forest mode is single-checkout permanently — keyless-minted first entries can never be authenticated by a later key); the marker records auth keyed/keyless; a keyless write into a keyed forest refuses in BOTH producers before touching anything; keyless-mode and pre-policy (field-less) markers keep working. Verify: node --test packages/gate-manifest/test/enable.test.mjs packages/tickets/test/manifest-segments.test.mjs --test-name-pattern=AC15.
AC14 — mint-time committability: with an ignore rule matching the branch-derived slug (e.g. .adlc/manifest.d/release-*.jsonl on branch release/1.0), the FIRST write on that branch throws before recording any evidence, in both producers. Verify: node --test packages/gate-manifest/test/segment-writer.test.mjs packages/tickets/test/manifest-segments.test.mjs --test-name-pattern=AC14.

PROCESS NOTES FOR THE IMPLEMENTING AGENT. (1) docs/specs/segmented-gate-manifest.md is itself declared a frozen rail by an earlier ticket, so rails-guard-ci will flag the spec edit on the PR; per repository practice that check requires the documented override path for spec-amending tickets — plan for it rather than being surprised. (2) Do not edit any existing ticket's body in .adlc/tickets/ as part of this work; rails-guard-ci rejects any change to an existing ticket's contract in a PR. (3) The mutation-gate rewrites prose inside string literals; if the enable command's error text trips it, reword the text — never pin it with a source-text test. (4) Run the FULL suite before pushing, not a package subset.
title: Make single-file vs segmented gate-manifest an explicit dual-mode choice: greenfield enable command, permanent-mode spec reframe, and an explicit threat model
